authorizedScope: new pure cursor timestamp helper and focused tests
criteria: Date-based cursor boundaries retain canonical PostgreSQL UTC timestamp text with six fractional digits, not JSDate millisecond truncation. Public displayed timestamps may remain millisecond ISO.

Mounted real PostgreSQL three-record fixtures with same millisecond/distinct microseconds return each row exactly once across limit1 pages in ASC comment/cardactivity and DESC trash/projectactivity/workspaceactivity/notifications feeds.
Forged cursor impossible Gregorian dates, zero year, invalid clock, invalid formats/types/oversized text produce controlled400/409 validation before SQL; no generic500 or internal detail.

Cursor always binds actual actor and resource/filter scope. Current authorization is checked on every page. Reusing another resource/actor/filter cursor returns private controlled4xx; no signature/possession is treated as authority.
New comments/trash cursor versions may reject ambiguous old cursors with409 refresh. Existing activity/notification v2 shapes stay compatible with valid strict UTC timestamp values.

Project lists are lexical name/id, not date-based. New cursor binds actor + exact workspace or selected-project scope; malformed/ambiguous old/mismatched cursor returns400 INVALID_CURSOR rather than silently restarting. Do not load all projects to derive a context hash.
Preserve real query ordering/tiebreaker, bounded LIMIT, role/board locks and response envelopes; no row skipping, dropped assertions, changed trash cutoff or resurrected access.
Retain failing mounted baselines before edits. Run targeted PG cases, typecheck/contracts and nearest relevant suites after primary reservation; no approval/score/featureclosure.
requiredProof: Three microsecond-spaced rows in one millisecond, including tied timestamp+id tiebreak control, walk both sort directions to exhaustion and compare exactIDs.
At least two actors and two projects/cards; forged cursor parsed from actual priorpage; assert no new data on denial.
Project same-name/id lexical tie walk, workspace/actor/project scope mismatch and invalid cursor tests.
